einzeiler: Thor Pedersen shares his epic decade-long journey visiting every country without flying
kurzfassung: Thor Pedersen recounts his unprecedented journey of visiting every country in the world without taking a single flight. He discusses the logistical nightmares, including being stranded in Hong Kong during the pandemic, and how human connection ultimately mattered most. After nearly ten years on the road, he reflects on the difficult transition back to normal life and family.
stichpunkte: Thor Pedersen became the first person to visit all 203 countries without flying, starting the project in 2013.
The trip took nearly ten years, lasting nine years, nine months, and 16 days instead of the originally planned four years.
His travels were severely disrupted by an Ebola epidemic in West Africa and a two-year COVID-19 lockdown in Hong Kong.
He navigated South America extensively by bus, including a grueling 42-hour bus ride in Brazil on a strict budget of $20 a day.
While stranded in Hong Kong, he coped with isolation by setting extreme hiking goals, such as scaling the region's highest peaks.
A donor in Florida funded his visit to Palau's jellyfish lake, which he describes as one of his most extraordinary lifetime experiences.
He finally completed his quest in May 2023 by reaching the Maldives as his final destination.
Adjusting to normal life after returning home proved intensely difficult after a decade of having a singular travel identity.

clips.hook: Discovering that no one had ever visited every country without flying
clips.text: The realization that nobody had accomplished global travel entirely without aviation hit like a heavy blow, especially given that almost every other major exploration milestone had already been achieved.

clips.hook: Knowing every country's sequence while having no idea how to cross borders
clips.text: The traveler mapped out the exact chronological sequence of every single nation he would visit long in advance, despite having zero clue what obstacles awaited him at each border.

clips.hook: The most essential item and the strangest place to fall asleep
clips.text: A simple pen proved to be the most vital gear for the entire decade-long expedition, while resting atop a truck in Congo stands out as the most bizarre sleeping spot.

clips.hook: Learning about a viral outbreak in Wuhan while arriving in Hong Kong
clips.text: After completing a twelve-day ocean voyage, the captain handed out face masks and casually mentioned a dangerous new virus spreading in a distant Chinese city that nobody on board had previously heard of.

clips.hook: A decade of repetitive routines felt like getting brainwashed
clips.text: Repeating the exact same micro-tasks for nearly ten years ultimately reshaped his entire personality, replacing his true self with the permanent identity of the global traveler.

beschreibung:
Thor Pedersen is the first person to visit every country in the world without flying. That is 203 countries by land and sea. He sits down with Kelly to unpack his epic quest, which he chronicled in his book, The Impossible Journey.
